newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania fund manager plans first closed-end fund.
newsitem.headline: Romania fund manager plans first closed-end fund.

text.p: Romanian investment fund manager Quantum SA said on Monday it planned to turn its Investor SA into the country's first closed-end fund to make long-term investments in mass privatisation shares.
"Such private closed-end funds, which are venture capital funds, are badly needed to invest in mass selloff shares on the long term," Quantum president Ioana Vlas said.
A mass privatisation process started last year has offered up to 60 percent of shares in 3,905 companies to some 17 million adult Romanians in exchange for vouchers and coupons.
Romania now has 12 investment funds, all of the open-ended type.

The sector was shaken when the largest trust, FMOA, fell 45 percent or $71 million in worth following a March rule by capital market regulator CNVM compelling funds to report actual net assets rather than projected values.
The new rule triggered falls at most unit trusts with depositors rushing to redeem their units. FMOA and then another big investment fund, Credit Fond, were suspended for 90 days.

Quantum, which is now authorised to administer open-ended funds, will seek approval from CNVM to administer Investor in the closed-end variant, Vlas said. If Quantum gets approval Investor will become Romania's first closed-end fund.

"The advantage of the the closed-end fund is that it does not need to keep a certain level of liquidity and therefore it can make long-term investments in shares which are not very liquid when it buys them," she said. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
